etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English wepen, from Old English wēpan (“to weep, complain, bewail, mourn over, deplore”), from Proto-West Germanic *wōpijan, from Proto-Germanic *wōpijaną (“to weep”), from Proto-Indo-European *weh₂b- (“to call, cry, complain”).

Cognate with Scots wepe, weip (“to weep”), Saterland Frisian wapia (“to cry, complain”), Icelandic æpa (“to yell, shout”).

definitions.definition: To cry; to shed tears, especially when accompanied with sobbing or other difficulty speaking, as an expression of emotion such as sadness or joy.

quote.citation: 1847 November 1, Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, Evangeline, a Tale of Acadie, Boston, Mass.: William D. Ticknor & Company, →OCLC, part I:
1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Numbers 11:13:
quote.text: They weep unto me, saying, Give us flesh, that we may eat.

definitions.definition: (medicine, of a wound or sore) To produce secretions.
To flow in drops; to run in drops.

quote.citation: c. 1596–1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Second Part of Henry the Fourth, […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act IV, scene iii]:
quote.text: The blood weeps from my heart.

definitions.definition: To give off moisture in small quantities, e.g. due to condensation.
To hang the branches, as if in sorrow; to be pendent; to droop; said of a plant or its branches.
(obsolete, transitive) To weep over; to bewail.

quote.text: Fair Venus wept the sad disaster  Of having lost her favorite dove.

quote.citation: 1850, [Alfred, Lord Tennyson], In Memoriam, London: Edward Moxon, […], →OCLC, Canto XIII, page 20:
quote.text: […] Which weep a loss for ever new,⁠A void where heart on heart reposed;⁠And, where warm hands have prest and closed,Silence, till I be silent too.

quote.citation: 1897, Bram Stoker, Dracula, New York: Doubleday & McClure, published 1899, page v. 62:
quote.text: He's coming, too, and we both want to mingle our weeps over the wine-cup[.]

definitions.definition: A red or reddish liquid that seeps out from raw muscular meat during storage, consisting mostly of water and protein; "meat juice".
A lapwing; wipe, especially, a northern lapwing (Vanellus vanellus).
